title: Introduce KV mesh balancer and fragmentation sentinel for continuous batching
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: On high-concurrency workloads with continuous batching we observe growing KV cache fragmentation on GPUs: many small holes and stranded tokens reduce effective cache capacity, raising per-token latency and evictions under load. Existing slab/coalescer approaches either introduce large background pauses or require locking patterns that increase CPU overhead and throttle batch throughput.

Goal: Design and ship a low-overhead KV allocation strategy plus background mitigation (the 'KV mesh balancer' + 'fragmentation sentinel') that reduces fragmentation by 30-50% under representative PLG workloads while keeping steady-state CPU overhead < 6% and tail latency impact < 5ms p95. The solution must be safe for hot models (large KV footprints), compatible with continuous batching, and feature-flagged for canary rollouts on Dedicated nodes.

High-level approach:
- KV mesh balancer: partition GPU KV pool into many small micro-domains (mesh tiles) that can be independently reclaimed/compacted. Allocation favors placing entries from the same request/batch into a small set of tiles to increase locality for streaming KV reuse. When a request's KV set crosses tiles, the balancer will prefer tiling with affinity heuristics derived from token fingerprinting and recent access traces.
- Fragmentation sentinel: lightweight telemetry agent that tracks per-tile slack (bytes wasted), live occupancy, and fragmentation velocity (change in slack over time). When a tile's slack exceeds a dynamic threshold, the sentinel marks it as a candidate for opportunistic relocation.
- Opportunistic relocation: perform fine-grained async copies of hot entries from high-slack tiles into denser tiles during low-GPU-usage windows. Use epoched soft-locks and write-once relocation buffers to avoid global freezes. Relocation is throttled by GPU utilization signals and continuous-batching latency guardrails.
- Deferred micro-compaction: for cold/abandoned tiles, perform background compaction with incremental GPU kernels that sweep only marked tiles at a rate proportional to fragmentation velocity.
- Eviction policy integration: extend the eviction heuristic to prefer freeing entire low-density tiles first (tile-first eviction) when under memory pressure, to reduce scattering.

Trade-offs considered:
- CPU vs GPU work: relocation and sentinel bookkeeping incur CPU cycles; we limit CPU overhead by batching sentinel updates and using compact counters.
- Latency vs capacity: aggressive relocation reduces fragmentation at cost of transient latency and copy bandwidth; we bound this via utilization thresholds and p95 latency checks.
- Complexity vs reliability: the mesh introduces indirection; to avoid correctness bugs we adopt simple tile metadata with versioned descriptors and a conservative rollback path for failed relocations.

Metrics and success criteria:
- Fragmentation ratio (total slack / allocated pool) target: reduce from baseline by >= 30% on avg workload and >= 20% on worst-case traces.
- Effective cache hit-rate improvement: +4-8% for chat shading workload.
- CPU overhead (scheduler + sentinel): < 6% of core cycles on an inference node.
- Tail latency delta: p95 change < +5ms; p99 rollback threshold triggers immediate pause.

Compatibility and safety:
- Feature-flagged per-cluster with runtime knobs: tile_size, relocation_window_ms, sentinel_threshold_pct, cpu_quota_pct.
- Rollback: atomic tile descriptor versioning ensures in-progress relocations can be invalidated and original pointers preserved until commit.
- Telemetry: dashboard panels for tile slack distribution, relocation rate, compaction throughput, and per-model KV pressure.

Implementation plan (phases):
1) Prototype (2w): implement mesh metadata and allocation affinity in dev build; add sentinel counters; unit tests for descriptor versioning.
2) Bench harness (1w): synthetic fragmentation traces + continuous-batching benchmark to measure overhead and benefits.
3) Canary (2w): deploy to 5 Dedicated nodes with opt-in customers; enable telemetry and a kill-switch.
4) Gradual rollout (4w): expand to 20% capacity, monitor thresholds, tune heuristics.
5) GA (post verification): merge and include in runtime-1.22 release.

Rollout safety knobs:
- global_feature_override boolean (server side)
- per-node relocation_bandwidth_limit_mb
- latency_guard_ms (if exceeded -> pause relocation)

Open questions / unknowns:
- Optimal tile size trade-offs between relocation granularity and metadata overhead. Initial guess: 64-256KB tiles. Need experiments.
- How aggressive to be with merging small hot fragments without impacting KV access patterns during continuous batching.

Deliverables:
- PR with mesh allocator and sentinel (runtime repo)
- Confluence design doc + measurement results
- Dashboard panels and alerts

comments: 2026-03-02 - Prototype started: created mesh metadata and basic allocation path. Initial microbench shows allocation latency +0.8%.
2026-03-04 - Sentinels added: we aggregate per-tile slack with a 1s emit window. Jordan reviewed and suggested coalescing counters to reduce cache-line contention.

2026-03-06 - Bench results (local): synthetic fragmentation trace shows 38% reduction in slack at tile_size=128KB, CPU overhead measured ~4.2% on c5-like control plane. Artifacts: confluence/kv-mesh-proto (see links).
2026-03-09 - Design review with Leah (SRE) and Priya (Product): prioritized safe rollback and p99 guard. Leah requested an emergency kill-switch route in console. Added to rollout plan.
2026-03-11 - PR opened: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4217 - initial impl. Need kernel-level review for relocation kernels. Assigned to kernel team (Victor).

2026-03-13 - Integration test failing under extreme micro-batching: observed a spike in p99 when relocation started concurrently with large model KV flush. Mitigation: add relocation backoff when batch inflight > N. Follow-up task created.
Next steps: stabilize backoff heuristic, expand canary config, add more dashboard alerts for fragmentation velocity and relocation-induced latency.
